newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Economist wants Romania gvt to boost capital mkts.
newsitem.headline: Economist wants Romania gvt to boost capital mkts.

text.p: A leading Romanian economist from the ruling centrist coalition called on Tuesday for a greater role of the government in supporting the growth of domestic capital markets.

"The most important goal is to unify the financial-banking market through cooperation between the government, National (central) Bank and the National Securities Commission," Varujan Vosganian, head of the Senate Budget, Finance and Banking Commission, said in an interview in the economic weekly Bursa.
"This calls for a new attitude of the central bank, which at the moment wants to control all financial flows, and which has done nothing to develop capital markets," Vosganian said.

Vosganian's Romanian Alternative (AR) party is a member of the Democratic Convention bloc -- senior partners in the coalition government which took office following the centrists' election win over the leftists last November.
"The government should also assume the task of developing the capital market, which it hasn't done so far," he said.
The growth of capital markets is a plank of reforms agreed with the International Monetary Fund in exchange for new loans.
Vosganian called for a greater role of the state to rebuild confidence in investment funds, hit by a crisis last year when some schemes failed to make promised payments to depositors.
"State banks could, for instance, buy investment paper, so that the population may see that the state has a financial stake and that the future of their investments is guaranteed."

Romania should also expand its bonds market, Vosganian said, arguing for financial investment companies should have a share in primary distribution of bills and for public access to bourse operations.
